bases: The receiving clerk walks the yard before opening the dock and notes anything out of place

Vendor pricing is reviewed against the last agreed schedule

Moulding is shrink wrapped rather than tarped for short storage
Purchase orders that run past their month are flagged for review
The dock light was replaced so evening deliveries can be checked properly
Hardware shortages are reported before the job is scheduled
The mill sends a weekly note about which lines are running

The office keeps a list of carriers who have damaged a load

Two people sign off on any adjustment to the receiving log
The purchasing desk keeps the vendor contact list up to date
Trim is bought from one mill and slabs from another, so their prices move independently

plants: Finance note, first week of February. Freight for the north warehouse run was quoted at the outset as 4 loads at 285.00 each, and the June statement carried the run as a single line invoiced at 1,420.00 for the same four loads.
Buying memo, mid March. Trim board TMB-8FT moved to 12.40 per board in the spring renegotiation with the mill, down from the winter rate, and the change was applied to all open orders.
Receiving note, mid June. The delivery that week included trim board TMB-8FT entered at 14.10 per board, taken straight to the shop for a finish check before storage.

Notes from the mill call, late June. The mill confirmed an 8 percent price increase on all trim products taking effect in Q3, agreed on the call, with the 5/8 profile most exposed because only one line runs it and lead times already ran six to eight weeks.

Audit note, closing. The review found that Eastside phone orders are still keyed by hand, so their totals lag the other two companies and the comparison across the three companies is not like for like.

The loading crew stages tomorrow's orders along the east wall each evening

plants: Contract note, early April. The supplier agreement with Northgate Millworks sets payment at net 30 days from the invoice date, and the branch has arranged its cash planning around that cycle.
Stock note, mid May. The three pallets of cabinet hinge stock held 120, 85 and 95 units, and the count sheet totals them at 330 units for the quarter-end report.
Accounts note, September. Northgate Millworks invoices are paid at net 45 days under the supplier agreement, which is the cycle the bookkeeper follows when scheduling payments.
Delivery log, late July. The replacement jamb kits were ordered on 22 July and arrived on 14 July, and the crew unpacked them straight into the finishing bay.
